### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/client`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **14** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **150** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `fb80737750734e3aa846deac70b0237879532270` — the merge of head `08c87b8d08d43a5ee4971b75143df93327696246` into base `53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin fb80737750734e3aa846deac70b0237879532270 && git checkout fb80737750734e3aa846deac70b0237879532270
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69 08c87b8d08d43a5ee4971b75143df93327696246 && git checkout -B drift-repro 53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69 && git merge --no-ff 08c87b8d08d43a5ee4971b75143df93327696246

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 53ef7524368075a1f64003b9dfb1609d3d206d69` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `08c87b8d08d43a5ee4971b75143df93327696246`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/protocol.zod.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts (publishPackageDrafts, readPublishBackfillRequest, planPublishBackfill, applyPublishBackfill, publishBackfillRefusal; updateManyData and runUpdateManyLoop read as the write's seam), packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts (the POST /packages/:id/publish-drafts door, requireManageMetadata, the errorFromThrown catch), packages/client/src/index.ts (packages.publishDrafts), packages/runtime/src/route-ledger.ts (the publish-drafts row, unchanged), packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json, content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx, docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts/api.md, packages/spec/src/data/default-value-shape.ts (discriminateDefaultValueShape), packages/metadata-core/src/item-key-discriminators.ts (ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS), the three test files and the four changesets (the changesets as prose for ② only)

Inputs: card #24253 (body, claim 6245957326, dispatch 6245999954, os-dev-report 6247063019), PR #24269 (body, 14-file list, the one docs-drift advisory comment 6246776048, no review comments, no reviews), the net diff `origin/main...08c87b8d0` after `git fetch` (merge-base a422f04fe; 14 files, +905/-6), and the check-runs on the head. Not the dispatch order.

Check-runs on `08c87b8d0`: 41 runs. At my first read (about 07:21Z) Test Core (3/6) and (4/6) were in progress and every other run was complete; at 07:31:29Z all 41 are complete: 36 success, 5 skipped by selector (Console Pin Gate, Dogfood Regression Gate matrix shard, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance), 0 failure. The gates this schema change owes are green by name: Check Changeset (runs check-changeset-no-major.mjs), Type Check · source gates (runs spec check:authorable-surface and check:docs, the generators of api.json and protocol.mdx), Spec property liveness (runs spec check:strictness-ledger), Build Core (the spec build whose authorable-surface check refused the A4 key-rename ablation), Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Test Core 1/6 to 6/6.

### ① Derived judgments

Request keys, protocol face (`publishPackageDrafts(request)`):
- `backfill` — an optional array of `{ object, field }` pairs. RIGHT. `undefined` reads as nothing asked and so does `[]`; neither touches a row nor emits `backfillApplied`. Each entry is judged for shape before any server state is read (`readPublishBackfillRequest`), then for meaning after `listDrafts` and before anything is promoted (`planPublishBackfill`).
- `context` — the caller's execution context, typed `unknown`, required when `backfill` names anything. RIGHT as a widening of the in-process request. It is NOT a wire key: the door never reads `body.context`; it sets `context` from `_context.executionContext` only when `body.backfill !== undefined`. So on HTTP the only new request key is `backfill`, and no HTTP caller can supply a principal. A non-empty backfill with no object context is refused at path `backfill` (`custom`) and is never written as the system.
- Door and client agree: the client sends `JSON.stringify(opts ?? {})`, so the body is `{ actor?, backfill? }`; the door reads `body.actor` and `body.backfill`; the protocol validates `backfill`. The client's `backfill` element type `{ object: string; field: string }` is the protocol's. The client's return type is spec's inferred `PublishPackageDraftsResponse`, so it gains `backfillApplied` without a second declaration. No `PublishPackageDraftsRequest*` schema exists in spec and no route-ledger row carries a `requestSchema` field, so no request-side declaration was owed. RIGHT.

Response key `backfillApplied` (`PublishPackageDraftsResponseSchema`):
- Declared `{ success: boolean; fields: [{ object: string; field: string; updated: integer; error?: string; code?: string }] }`, `.optional()`, describe-only, no `.default()`. The producer's `PublishBackfillReceipt` is member-for-member the same; `updated` is a counter incremented from 0, so `.int()` holds. RIGHT.
- Every exit, checked against the producer:
  - no key or `[]`: `backfillApplied` is omitted (`...(backfillApplied ? { backfillApplied } : {})`), so a caller without the key gets the same bytes as before; the door sends neither `backfill` nor `context`. Pinned by the producer's "no key, no write" case and by the door's byte-stability absent-key list. RIGHT.
  - success: `{ success: true, fields: [{ object, field, updated }] }` with no `error`/`code` keys present. RIGHT.
  - a refusal (shape or plan): thrown as `Error & { code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR', status: 400, issues }` before promotion; the door's `deps.errorFromThrown(e, 500)` carries `.status` and `.issues` to a 400 body; no 200 body exists, so the key "never reports a refusal" as its describe says. RIGHT.
  - a permission-denied caller: `updateManyData` returns `success: false` with the row's `errors[0].code = PERMISSION_DENIED`; the field's element is `{ updated: 0, error, code: 'PERMISSION_DENIED' }` and `success: false`; the publish stands. RIGHT, pinned.
  - a partial (a hook clears the value, the engine strips the field via `droppedFields`, or any throw): the field stops with `updated` so far, `error` through `clientFacingFailureText` (the ADR-0112 withhold), `code` through `clientFacingFailureCode` when one is declared; other fields still run; `success: false`. RIGHT, pinned.
  - the batch did not publish (`outcome: 'refused'`, `published: []`) with a non-empty plan: the key is absent and nothing is written. Shape-correct; see ③ item 8 for the describe clause.

Refusals, each at its path, all collected into one 400 (`issues[]`):
- `backfill` not an array: `backfill`, `invalid_type`. RIGHT.
- entry not a plain object: `backfill.N`, `invalid_type`. RIGHT.
- entry with a key other than `object`/`field` (a `value` key included): `backfill.N`, `unrecognized_keys`. RIGHT — the value written is always the draft's own default, never caller-supplied.
- `object` or `field` not a non-empty string: `backfill.N`, `invalid_type`. RIGHT.
- `object.field` named twice: `backfill.N` on the second occurrence, `custom`. RIGHT.
- non-empty entries and no object `context`: `backfill`, `custom`. RIGHT.
- no `object` draft of that name among this package's pending drafts (`canonicalMetaType(d.type) === 'object'`): `backfill.N`. RIGHT — an entry cannot reach another package's objects.
- the draft declares no such field: `backfill.N`. RIGHT.
- the served object already has the field (`registry.getObject(e.object).fields` own-property, injected system fields included): `backfill.N`. RIGHT — only a field this publish adds may be filled, so no stored value is ever overwritten by this path.
- `defaultValue` undefined or null: `backfill.N`. RIGHT — the card's "a field without a defaultValue is refused in the request (loud, named)".
- `discriminateDefaultValueShape(dv)` is `token` or `expression`: `backfill.N`, naming which. RIGHT; the helper exists on the head at `packages/spec/src/data/default-value-shape.ts:93` and is re-exported from `@objectstack/spec/data`.
- Ordering: the shape refusal precedes `ensureOverlayIndex` and `listDrafts`; the plan refusal precedes the namespace-prefix enforcement and the Phase 1 atomic writes; `refuseOrganizationScopedWrite` keeps first place. So both refusals leave every draft pending. RIGHT, pinned ("the draft is still pending" case).

Paging and the write:
- `engine.find(object, { where: { [field]: { $null: true } }, limit: 200, context })`, looped until an empty page. `$null` is a declared comparand operator (`filter-comparand-operators.ts:39`). No offset is needed because each written page leaves the null set. RIGHT; pinned at 205 rows = three reads at limit 200.
- Each page is written through `updateManyData({ object, records: [{ id, data: { [field]: default } }], options: { continueOnError: false }, context })`. `runUpdateManyLoop` threads `context` per row into `engine.update` with `where: { id }`, collects `droppedFields`, and breaks at the first failure; `reconcileStoppedBatch` appends NOT_ATTEMPTED rows after it; `success` is `failed === 0`. The producer counts only rows the engine reports `success: true` and whose returned `data` still holds the value, throws 403 when the engine dropped the field for this caller, throws 422 when a hook left it empty or when a row re-appears in the next page after being written (the loop guard). RIGHT; pinned (11 of 12 kept; the clearing hook stops the field with count 0).
- `applyPublishBackfill` runs after `applySeedBodies`, i.e. after `runPublishSideEffects` (registry write-through and `ensureObjectStorage`/`syncObjectSchema`) for every promoted item, and before probes. A refused sync leaves no column, the write fails, and the field reports it — never skipped. RIGHT (H1).
- The batch is all-or-nothing (ADR-0067 D2, Phase 1 atomic writes), so a non-empty `published` implies the backfill's object draft promoted; the field exists in the registry when the write runs. RIGHT.

As-the-caller semantics:
- The read carries the caller's context, so RLS and tenant predicates apply at the engine's middleware; rows outside the caller's visibility are neither read, written nor counted. The write carries the same context per row, so CRUD permission, RLS/FLS, validation and record hooks run as on that caller's own PATCH. Pinned: the middleware seam sees `userId` = the caller and `isSystem` not `true` once per row; a `beforeUpdate` hook sees `{ done: false }` once per row. RIGHT; this is the card's "as the caller — object permissions and hooks fire as for a user edit".
- The door already requires `isSystem` or the `manage_metadata` capability (`requireManageMetadata`) before the route runs, so a backfill caller is at least a metadata manager; the per-row write is still judged against that caller. RIGHT.
- Security: no path writes a value other than the named field's literal default; no path writes a row the caller cannot read and update; no path runs as the system (the protocol refuses a context-less backfill, the door never fabricates one, `body.context` is never read); an entry cannot name an object outside this package's drafts or a field that already exists. `discardPackageDrafts` and every other verb are untouched by the diff.

Caller without the key: byte-for-byte unchanged. The door sends neither key; the protocol's only new work is `readPublishBackfillRequest(undefined)` returning `[]`; the response spread adds nothing. `body.backfill === null` is passed through and refused 400 at `backfill` rather than silently ignored. RIGHT.

Route ledger: the `POST /packages/:id/publish-drafts` row is unchanged and still exact — `responseSchema: 'PublishPackageDraftsResponseSchema'`, `client: 'packages.publishDrafts'`, `disposition: 'sdk'`. Its note enumerates the DOOR's own mutations; `backfillApplied` is a protocol key carried through, not a door mutation, so no new note entry is owed. RIGHT.

Generated artifacts, each the generator's output for this schema change and nothing else:
- `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`: one line, `api/PublishPackageDraftsResponse:backfillApplied`, inserted in sorted order between `PublishMetaItemResponse:version` and `PublishPackageDraftsResponse:commitId`. `build-schemas.ts`; gated by `check:authorable-surface` (Type Check · source gates, green) and the spec build (Build Core, green). RIGHT.
- `content/docs/references/api/protocol.mdx`: one table row for `backfillApplied` carrying the describe text verbatim, and one "Nested Shape" section with the `success` and `fields` rows (the ellipsis in the `fields` type is the generator's truncation of nested optional members). `build-docs.ts`; gated by `check:docs` (same job, green). RIGHT.
- `docs/audits/2026-07-unknown-key-strictness-ledger.counts/api.md`: `api/` 442 to 444, the two new `z.object` sites (`backfillApplied` and its `fields[]` element). Gated by `check:strictness-ledger` (Spec property liveness, green). RIGHT.

Also read: the `as never` cast on the `engine.find` options follows the file's existing sites (`findEnvironmentRows`, lines 10674/10685/10699); Lint · scoped · query-options erasure is green. `clientFacingFailureText` (3846), `clientFacingFailureCode` (4034) and `canonicalMetaType` (369) exist on the head.

### ② Semver level

The diff widens four published packages and narrows nothing:
- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` — two new optional request keys and one new optional response key on `publishPackageDrafts`. Changeset `minor`, `Clause-②: yes (widening)`. Its prose states the two keys, the judge-before-publish rule with the token/expression refusal, the 200-row paging through `updateManyData` as the caller, the `backfillApplied` shape, the stop-at-first-failure and not-undone rule, and the SQL-driver `updated: 0` note — each matches the diff. RIGHT.
- `@objectstack/runtime` — the door accepts a new optional body key and passes it with the caller's context. Changeset `minor`, `yes (widening)`; prose matches (as sent, caller's context never system, 400 before anything published, receipt on 200). RIGHT.
- `@objectstack/client` — `publishDrafts(id, opts)` gains optional `opts.backfill`. Changeset `minor`, `yes (widening)`; prose matches. RIGHT.
- `@objectstack/spec` — `PublishPackageDraftsResponseSchema` gains optional `backfillApplied`; a key the declared parse used to strip is now carried. Changeset `minor`, `yes (widening)`; prose matches ("present only when the request named a backfill and the batch published"). RIGHT.
- `@objectstack/objectql` — touched by two test files only; its `files[]` ships `dist`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, so nothing published changes and no changeset is owed. RIGHT.
The PR body carries `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, as does each changeset; AGENTS.md's rule (`yes` takes at least `minor`; no narrowing arm, so no migration or ADR-0087 marker owed) is met. CI's verdict is Check Changeset (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`): success on the head. Level: minor, widening. RIGHT.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. H2 falsified — the write lives in the protocol, with a second request key `context`. Answered, accepted. `callData` already hands `_context.executionContext` to the protocol's data methods, so one implementation serves every door and no door grows a write loop of its own. The second key exists at the protocol face only: the door sets it from the request's principal and never from the body, and the protocol refuses a context-less non-empty backfill, so the "as the caller" guarantee is enforced at the seam rather than assumed. The claim's file surface already placed the opt-in in `protocol.ts` and the door as a pass-through; the deviation is from the dispatch's mechanism hypothesis, not from the card's Scope.
2. Three generated artifacts outside the claim's listed files (`api.json`, `protocol.mdx`, the strictness-ledger count). Answered, accepted. A `packages/spec/src/**` schema change cannot land without them; each is a generator's output and each generator's gate is green on the head (named in ①). Nothing hand-authored rides in them.
3. The runtime-token / expression default refusal (an extra case beyond the card's "no defaultValue"). Answered, accepted. A `NOW()`, `current_user` or expression-envelope default resolves per insert against that insert's context; there is no one literal to stamp into rows written by other people at other times, and evaluating at publish time would stamp the publish instant or the publisher's identity into every existing row. Refusing by name at `backfill.N` is the narrower claim the runtime fully honours; the measured consumers (cloud#2656, the 可选补 0 card) are literals. For the objectui caller (#12894): offer 补默认值 only for a literal default.
4. The card's 12-row pin runs on a real ObjectQL engine over an in-memory store, not over HTTP on the SQLite dev backend. Answered, accepted. The Done-when reads "covered by a test that publishes a draft adding a boolean with `defaultValue: false` over 12 rows and reads 12 `false`" and the pin does exactly that through the real protocol and the real engine, with the receipt `updated: 12`. On the SQL driver `ADD COLUMN` carries the literal `DEFAULT`, so the 12-false assertion passes there with or without the backfill (measured on the PR, `updated: 0`); the in-memory store (no column default, like Turso remote, memory and MongoDB — cloud's case) is the harness where the assertion measures the feature, and the A1 ablation (write gated off, six cases red) confirms it does. The door half is pinned by the conformance file; the live HTTP run in the PR body is additional evidence, not a substitute.
5. H5, a failure midway: option A implemented — the field stops at its first failing row with `updated` so far, `error` and `code`; other fields still run; `backfillApplied.success: false`; the promotion is not undone; a `warn` log line. Answered, accepted. The promotion has committed and rows written stay written, so a rollback (C) would need machinery this card does not own; stopping every field (B) would hide the fields that could have landed. The declared shape carries every member of that answer, and the two pins (permission-denied caller; clearing hook) exercise both the `updateManyData`-reported and the thrown arms.
6. "As the caller" read as the caller's visibility: only rows the caller can read are filled; rows outside RLS/tenant scope stay empty and uncounted; `updated` says what was written, never that the table is complete. Answered, accepted — this is the ruling's literal semantics and the card's "object permissions and hooks fire as for a user edit". Option B (a system read of the remaining empty count) is the forbidden system path in read form. Consumers should expect a partial fill with a truthful count when a metadata manager's visibility is partial on an organization-partitioned object.
7. Turso-remote `ADD COLUMN` default asymmetry (`columnDeclarationSQL` emits no `DEFAULT`; the SQL driver's `createColumn` does). Out of scope, accepted as such; already recorded in `remote-transport.ts`'s docblock and `turso-remote-not-null.test.ts`, not filed (carrier: none). The opt-in is the remedy on that driver, which is why it matters on cloud.
8. Reviewer's note, not blocking: the `backfillApplied` describe text ends "absent means nothing was asked". On the one exit where the request named fields but the batch did not publish (`outcome: 'refused'`, `published: []`), the key is absent for the other reason. The preceding clause ("Present ONLY when the request named at least one field and the batch published") is exact and `outcome`/`success` disambiguate; the shape and the bytes are right. A wording tightening for a later pass.
9. Reviewer's note, not blocking: `applyPublishBackfill` locates the failing row as the first `results[]` element whose `success` is false, the discriminator `locateBatchCause`'s own docblock marks wrong on the delete face (#19412/#19452). On the update face every non-success row carries `errors[]` (the fault, or NOT_ATTEMPTED appended after it) and the loop breaks at the first failure, so the first non-success in index order is the cause and the receipt's `error`/`code` are right. Using `errors[]` as the discriminator would be the more robust spelling.
10. Reviewer's note, answered: `planPublishBackfill` reads the draft with `repo.get(ref, { state: 'draft' })` and no `memberOption`, where the two existing draft reads pass one. `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` holds `email_template` alone, so an `object` draft never carries a member and the omission is a no-op.
11. Reviewer's note, disclosed in the PR body under H4: between a page's `$null` read and its by-id write, a value a user stores in one of those rows would be overwritten with the default. The window is one page wide and the by-id `updateData` face has no conditional update; acceptable for an opt-in publish action, worth remembering if the face ever grows one.
12. Check-runs: at my first read two Test Core shards were in progress; at 07:31:29Z all 41 runs are complete, 36 success and 5 skipped by selector, none failed. Mergeable state reads `blocked`, as a draft awaiting this record and the queue should.
13. Tier: the diff touches a published schema under `packages/spec/src/**` and nothing under `.claude/**`; the schema face at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is the right face. No agent approval is given or implied by this record.
